newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX recovers from Thursday's decline.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX recovers from Thursday's decline.

text.p: The Hungarian share market more than regained Thursday's losses on Friday in quiet trading, traders said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 6,784.66 points, up 53.09 points or 0.79 percent.
"In the early part of the session some investors believed that Thursday's falls would continue but after a while they began to buy stocks constituting the BUX index's basket," one trader said.

Retailer Fotex led gainers by a more than 26 percent rise to 220 forints in just a few minutes as a result of which the bourse suspended its trading for the rest of the session for an excessive rally.
Oil and gas company MOL finished at 4,205 forints, down 50.

Chemicals TVK ended at 3,345 forints, up 50. The company announced this morning that privatisation agency APV will pay 4.40 billion forints of privatisation revenue and an additional 842 million of accumulated interest to it.
One analyst said she expected a correction to come on the market within one month.

"I base my opinion on trends on the futures market as interest rate contents are very low," said Gabriella Bor of New York Broker Budapest. "For example the September BUX has an interest content of 12.86 percent and this is far below yields on the government securities."
Benchmark three-, six- and twelve-month government papers yield around 20 percent.
Bor added investors were hesitant to open selling positions on the BUX futures market.
